data.analysis: Keep N=3 and all role identities, but sharpen the experiments to distinguish team-startup overhead, SIMD strategy, and temporal reuse. T1 should contrast per-step OpenMP teams with a persistent team; T2 should contrast compiler auto-vectorization with target-supported explicit SIMD; T3 should compare temporal blocking against a spatial-only control. This reduces overlap and tests competing explanations. The source and baseline do not establish whether the kernel is compute- or bandwidth-limited, whether GCC already vectorizes it, or whether four-thread scaling helps; treat these as hypotheses. The correct baseline has three measured times with mean 0.464905 seconds, but no separate one-/four-core results are supplied.

revisions.objective: Replace the serial sweeps with OpenMP work over disjoint rows or slabs, honoring the threads argument as a CPU budget. Compare a team created for each timestep with a persistent team spanning all six steps, measuring any fork/join savings against synchronization and buffer-parity handling. Ensure workers finish each timestep before the next reads its output. Preserve full initialization, update bounds, and boundaries. Test correctness and native wall time at one and four cores, including initialization and overhead.
revisions.subject: Compare per-step and persistent OpenMP teams

revisions.objective: Optimize the contiguous-x radius-3 update, contrasting a compiler-vectorizable loop with explicit SIMD only when supported by the frozen target configuration. Do not change compiler settings or assume row alignment; handle tails and generic n. Preserve the recurrence, full initialization, and boundaries, and validate the fixed tolerance. Measure both core budgets and include any setup costs.
revisions.subject: Contrast compiler auto-vectorization and target-supported SIMD

revisions.objective: Focus on temporal reuse across the six dependent steps. Compare a spatial-only tiled control with a halo-aware multi-step tile, holding the spatial kernel and threading strategy fixed within the comparison to isolate temporal reuse. Respect radius-three dependencies, produce both full output buffers with baseline initialization and boundaries, and include scratch allocation in timing. Avoid benchmark-size specialization; validate correctness and measure one- and four-core wall time.
revisions.subject: Isolate temporal blocking from spatial-only cache blocking

Compare measured programs under the unchanged protocol at one and four cores, including initialization and scratch costs; preserve correctness for all valid inputs and seeds, the stated tolerance, and generic dimensions.
